question.problem: Evaluate ${\int }_{C}\frac{x}{y}\,dx+\frac{y}{x}\,dy,$ where $C$ is a portion of the ellipse $r(t)=\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j$ for $t\in [0,\frac{\pi }{2}].$
question.worked_solution:
Along the curve, we have

$$
x(t)=\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,y(t)=2\operatorname{sin}⁡t.
$$

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,j \\  & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now evaluate the line integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}\frac{x}{y}\,dx+\frac{y}{x}\,dy & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\frac{x}{y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,dt+\frac{y}{x}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}(\frac{x}{y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\frac{y}{x}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡t}{2\operatorname{sin}⁡t}\cdot (-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)+\frac{2\operatorname{sin}⁡t}{\operatorname{cos}⁡t}\cdot (2\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t+4\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,dt \\  & ={-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡t-4\operatorname{cos}⁡t|}_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & =[-\frac{1}{2}-0]-[0-4] \\  & =\frac{7}{2}\end{aligned}
$$
